```{r, include=FALSE}
#libraries + reproducibility
set.seed(44)
library(ISLR) ## data package
library(tidyverse) ## data manipulation
library(tidymodels) ## tidy modeling
library(knitr) ## tables
library(rpart.plot) ## plotting trees
#install.packages("randomForest")
library(randomForest)
#install.packages("ranger")
library(ranger)
library(vip) ## bagging 
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
#cleaning the data and dividing it into training and test
PCOS_infertility <- read_csv("/data/accounts/fa26/nicolamalatestafa26/DSCI445/dsci445project/PCOS_infertility.csv")

PCOS_cleaned <- drop_na(PCOS_infertility)
PCOS_cleaned$PCOS <- as.factor(PCOS_cleaned$`PCOS (Y/N)`)
PCOS_cleaned$`PCOS (Y/N)` <- NULL



#splits
PCOS_splits <- initial_split(PCOS_cleaned, prop=0.75)
PCOS_training <- training(PCOS_splits)
PCOS_testing <- testing(PCOS_splits)
```



## Fitting the Decision Tree model: Non-Pruned
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
#spec
tree_spec <- decision_tree(
  mode="classification",
  engine="rpart")

#recipe
tree_recipe <- recipe(PCOS ~ ., data=PCOS_training)

tree_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(tree_recipe) |> add_model(tree_spec) 

tree_fit <- fit(tree_wf, data=PCOS_training)

#metrics
metric <- metric_set(accuracy)
tree_pred <- augment(tree_fit, new_data = PCOS_testing)
tree_pred |> metric(truth=PCOS, estimate=.pred_class) 

#plot
tree_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine() |>
  rpart.plot(roundint=FALSE)

#calculating the test error 
augment(tree_fit, new_data=PCOS_testing) |> metric(truth=PCOS, estimate=.pred_class)


```

Accuracy of around 62.5%, so a test error rate of around 37.5%. Not great...


## Pruned Tree & Determining Tree Complexity via 10-fold CV 

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#tree recipe
tree_recipe2 <- recipe(PCOS ~ ., data=PCOS_training)


tree_engine2 <- decision_tree(
  mode="classification",
  engine="rpart", 
  cost_complexity = tune()) #this is the complexity to be chosen

tree_wf2 <- workflow() |> add_recipe(tree_recipe2) |> add_model(tree_engine2) 

#degree to choose from 
cost_complexity_grid <- grid_regular(
  cost_complexity(range = c(-5, -1)), 
  levels = 40
)

#folds
set.seed(44)
cv_2 <- vfold_cv(PCOS_training, v=10)


final_tree_cv<- tree_wf2 |> tune_grid(resamples=cv_2, 
                  grid=cost_complexity_grid,
                  metrics=metric_set(accuracy))


best_alpha <- select_best(final_tree_cv, metric="accuracy")
best_alpha

#finally fitting with alpha= 0.00943
final_tree_wf <- finalize_workflow(tree_wf2, best_alpha)

final_tree_fit <- fit(final_tree_wf, data=PCOS_cleaned)

final_tree_fit |>
  extract_fit_engine() |>
  rpart.plot(roundint=FALSE)


#calculating the test error 
augment(final_tree_fit, new_data=PCOS_testing) |> metric(truth=PCOS, estimate=.pred_class)

final_tree_fit |> augment(new_data=PCOS_testing) |> conf_mat(truth=PCOS, estimate=.pred_class)


```
With using 10-fold CV to choose the exact level of complexity, then the test error is of around $1-0.91176=0.08824$, which is way lower than the non-pruned tree done above.  




## Bagging Tree
```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#spec 
bagging_spec <- rand_forest(trees=500) |> ## automatically grabs the number of columns
  set_engine("ranger", importance="impurity") |> ## save information to plot importance
  set_mode("classification")

#recipe stays as is for the tree model
bagging_recipe <- recipe(PCOS ~ ., data=PCOS_training)

bagging_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(bagging_recipe) |> add_model(bagging_spec) 

bagging_fit <- fit(bagging_wf, data=PCOS_training)

# importance
bagging_fit |> 
  extract_fit_parsnip() |>
  vip(num_features = 20)

```
